coverage_assessment: Sixteen Spanish- and English-language searches captured 409 ordered result headers and 64 source cards; the search tools exposed no total-result counts. Coverage included a general country-month search, focused sector/state searches, and weekly windows: Q003/Q014 for Jan 1–7, Q006 for Jan 8–14, Q016 for Jan 15–21, and Q008–Q012 for Jan 22–31, with additional topic and episode follow-ups. Regional, local-outlet, and sector coverage remains uneven; the windows do not prove exhaustive coverage. Eight candidates remain, including a newly body-verified Jan 20 Caracas Public Ministry gathering (E009); its demand is directed to a domestic state institution, but no individual turnout estimate or crowd description establishes 50 people, so it remains pending_threshold. Same-publisher S021 may overlap S022, and search-only S019 may describe the same action; neither is counted as independent confirmation or an additional event. S018’s contemporaneous pre-access denial scan covered only 29 unit cards and 2,326 coordinator checks, not the complete saved source universe; this cannot be retroactively cured by later scans. One search-only out-of-period lead is excluded and no continuation is assigned. S061, a later Diario de Los Andes legal update opened by ordinary HTTPS after a web Cache miss and DNS failure, reports a Jan 28 Trujillo labor demonstration and four detentions but does not establish attendance, exact venue, public accessibility, event-specific state target, physical end, or independence from S010; S010 contains conflicting detention context. Jan 15 and Jan 23 thresholds and local/national boundaries remain unresolved. Adjacent December and February search-only leads are not linked physically to January episodes. OVCS/NGO monthly and annual totals are coverage context, not simultaneous attendance or eligible unique-event counts. Actual 403 denials for S026, S048, S052, and S057 are respected without retries or alternate body access; S052 concerns a Jan 23 UCV story, not S022. S057’s report writer and relation to E004/E008 remain unknown and its search preview is not event evidence. S050 and S048 share same-event/overlapping-detail context, but written-origin independence remains unresolved despite different publishers/bylines; S050 is not independent corroboration and was used only for outside-month header metadata. No absence or exhaustive-coverage claim is made.
